goal: Replace the community-template import path's eager per-slot hydration fan-out with one Active-Manifest-bound, backend-resolved import snapshot, so a player can import a real observed template promptly without weakening canonical enhancement editability, observed-only policy, or Resolver authority.
userValue: A player taps a community template once, immediately sees the imported gear and its verified selected gems, enchants and embellishments, and can then edit a chosen slot normally. The action must not appear frozen for 15–30 seconds or silently lose enhancement selections after request timeout.
nonGoals: No change to the public observed-only community-template policy or introduction of baseline/recommended_bis templates into the public import entry.
No runtime Battle.net, Raider.IO, SimC, Wowhead or other external request during template import, gear edit or Resolve.
No client-authored raw enhancement value, forged option identity, client legality decision or client-derived socket capacity becomes authoritative.
No Gear/Community Release generation, Manifest pointer, PostgreSQL schema, scheduled sync, backfill, cleanup or production-data write change.
No removal or semantic change to the existing mode=initial and mode=slot public gear endpoints; ordinary slot editing remains lazy.
No worker-count-only, cache-size-only or sequential-request workaround presented as the product fix.
No merge before final candidate API/runtime parity, cold/warm import evidence and real WeChat verification.

currentTruth.historicalContractBoundary: Community Enhancement Editability v2 is completed and archived. Its editable canonical-selection contract remains mandatory, but its client-side all-affected-slot hydration implementation is not a current performance contract.

facts: The affected Elemental Shaman import issued one initial request followed by twelve mode=slot requests; the client starts affected slot hydration through Promise.all.
The gear endpoint limits all builds with a global four-worker semaphore while each client request has a 30000 ms timeout.

A cold compact finger1 slot build against the effective production environment took 3.731 seconds; a warm compact slot response took 0.097 seconds and transferred 625921 bytes before compression or 40282 bytes compressed.
The active release contains 27949 variants and 19201 source rows; a slot build constructs a release-backed catalog fragment rather than a lightweight option lookup.
The current in-process gear-payload LRU has eighty entries and its key includes class, spec, compact, mode and slot.
unprovenUntilInstrumentation: The exact incident cache hit or miss state cannot be reconstructed because the current runtime exposes no gear-payload cache hit metric.
The split between semaphore queue time, release reads, canonical shaping, Resolve and JSON serialization is not emitted by the current endpoint.
No claim is made that PostgreSQL base query time alone caused the incident.

contract.success: One compact import snapshot contains the validated public template identity, selected gear display records, canonical selected enhancement identities and labels, a matching Resolver snapshot/signature, manifest identity, bounded unresolved-type counts and plain recovery warnings. It contains no raw unrecognized enhancement value.
contract.failure: Missing, inapplicable, blocked, stale-manifest or unresolved import returns a structured problem. The client keeps its last verified configuration, shows a retryable plain message, and does not fall back to multi-slot hydration.
contract.performance: One import tap produces one community-import request. A later explicit edit may use the established single selected-slot lazy request; no background all-slot hydration is allowed.

mustChange: A pure backend community-template import projector reconciles a sealed winner template against one Active Manifest and invokes existing canonical Resolver ownership.

The release-store/cache read path loads only the selected winner's gear, variants, source evidence and option authority required by that import; it must not build the broad mode=slot catalog path once per affected slot.
The backend exposes the structured community-import route and bounded timing observability without exposing internal release rows, raw values or SQL details.

The mini-program uses the import route, commits only the matching verified snapshot and displays import progress; it no longer calls all affected mode=slot requests before applying a community template.
Focused backend/frontend tests characterize one-request import, canonical result parity, failure preservation, stale fencing and subsequent single-slot editing.
mustNotChange: Active public entry remains real-player observed templates only, with existing source and legality gates.
Active Manifest, immutable Gear/Community Releases, dependency vector, Resolver, Profile and stat-snapshot owners remain authoritative.
Existing mode=initial and mode=slot response semantics remain compatible for normal browse and editing flows.
Unknown enhancement values remain absent from Intent and user-visible only as bounded plain coverage warnings.
Duplicate gem occurrence order, replacement semantics, Resolve fencing and profile serialization remain lossless.
No sync, backfill, cleanup, pointer, schema or deployment-triggered async process runs as part of this change.
riskUnknown: Whether the present sealed Community Release provides every selected enhancement in a shape directly reusable by the Resolver, or needs one new pure reconciliation adapter.
The smallest cold-path latency achievable after targeted release reads until candidate Server-Timing evidence is recorded.
The exact compact payload fields needed by existing mini-program derived state without making the new endpoint a second general catalog endpoint.
evidenceRequired: Red-to-green tests prove one import request with no all-slot hydration, while later explicit editing requests at most the selected slot.
Pure/import/Resolver tests prove canonical selected values, unknown-value omission, duplicate occurrence preservation, exact manifest binding and structured failure behavior.
Candidate Server-Timing or structured timing evidence records queue, release read, reconciliation, Resolve, serialization and cache state for cold and warm imports.
Candidate deployment records final branch/commit/runtime file parity, PostgreSQL-only runtime, public observed-only parity, timer/backflow state, logs and code rollback path.

Real WeChat evidence proves the representative community template imports promptly, retains 8/8 gems, 6/8 enchants and 2/2 embellishments for the frozen Frost Mage fixture, then edits one selected slot normally.

ownership.factOwner: The new pure community-template import projector and server-side Resolver invocation own template-to-canonical selection reconciliation. Active Gear and Community Releases remain the only published source; server/gear_release_store.py owns scoped immutable reads and server/gear_runtime.py plus server/gear_resolver.py own final legality and resolved facts.
consumers: server/postgres_cache_store.py bounded immutable import-snapshot cache boundary
pages/builds/detail.js import serial, verified commit and selected-slot lazy editing
pages/builds/detail.wxml progress, retry and normal editor presentation

engineeringHealth.reason: The change touches the user-visible hot path plus news_backend.py, postgres_cache_store.py and release reads. It stays bounded through one purpose-built read model, a pure reconciliation owner, additive route/cache only, no write-path scope and explicit phase timing before performance claims.

acceptanceEvidence: New focused Python tests for the import projector, scoped release read, cache key/invalidation, route envelope and Server-Timing field shape.
New focused Node tests proving one community-import request, no all-slot hydration, visible progress, retry/failure preservation, stale import fencing and subsequent single-slot lazy detail loading.
Existing editable enhancement fixture tests retain Frost Mage 8/8 gems, 6/8 enchants and 2/2 embellishments, duplicate-gem occurrence semantics and unknown-value warning behavior.

One final PR-head candidate deployment, real HTTP cold/warm import timing, normal initial/slot compatibility smoke, 40-spec public observed-only shadow, timer/backflow/log checks and real WeChat import/edit proof.

decisionLog.decision: User approved continuing with the recommended atomic, backend-resolved community-template import direction after systematic read-only incident analysis.

The recommended fix is a purpose-built import contract, not increasing the global worker count, enlarging the existing generic LRU, serializing twelve requests, or weakening canonical enhancement semantics.
User reviewed the written Strict specification and approved progressing to the executable implementation plan; runtime implementation remains pending plan approval.
